thesis: Nvidia's own Q2 FY2027 release (26 Aug) reports revenue of $96.2B, up 106% year over year and 18% sequentially, with Data Center revenue of $89.0B, up 117% year over year, against a reported consensus of $86.33B; GAAP and non-GAAP gross margin were both 75.0%, and diluted EPS was $2.46 GAAP versus $2.22 non-GAAP (both figures given, GAAP the higher of the two). Management guided Q3 FY2027 revenue to $108.0B, an $11.8B sequential step-up. The 2.63x volume spike and the 8.7% close-to-close move on 27 Aug are the market absorbing that disclosure, not a technical event. The strongest counter-evidence is China: pre-earnings coverage put up to $5B of sales at risk from a single policy shift, and Bernstein has flagged circular financing among hyperscaler customers. That does not change the read, because the $11.8B sequential increase Nvidia has guided to is larger than the entire China exposure at risk, so the guided step-up does not depend on China holding. This suggests demand is being set by hyperscaler Blackwell Ultra deployment rather than by any single geography.
invalidation: Q3 FY2027 revenue tracks below the guided $108.0B, or a subsequent disclosure shows Data Center sequential growth decelerating rather than accelerating.

thesis: Held position. Microsoft's FQ4 2026 results (29 July) reported revenue of $90.01B against $87.62B expected and net income of $35.77B; EPS was $4.81 GAAP versus $4.74 adjusted (both reported, and here GAAP is the higher figure), against $4.24 expected on the adjusted basis, with revenue up about 18% year over year. Shares rose roughly 8% after hours, and the position has since carried a 37% 60-day move to a price 8.5% below its 52-week high. The strongest counter-evidence is regulatory: the FTC has widened its antitrust probe to cover cloud, AI and software bundling including Entra ID, cloud licensing terms and Copilot, Microsoft must face a UK mass claim worth up to $2.8B over Windows Server cloud licensing, and a shareholder suit alleges misleading Azure growth statements. That does not change the read for this holding period, because the FTC is reported to expect additional civil investigative demands rather than a public complaint before the end of 2026, so no adjudicated outcome falls before this position's next review. None of these proceedings surfaced a scheduled ruling, hearing, trial date or compliance deadline in the next ~90 days, so no active_litigation flag is set.
invalidation: The FTC converts the investigation into a filed complaint, or a subsequent quarter shows Azure/cloud revenue growth decelerating from the reported ~18% company-level pace.
sources: Insurance Journal (UK GBP2.8B cloud licensing claim): https://www.insurancejournal.com/news/international/2026/04/22/866800.htm
US Cloud (FTC antitrust probe scope and timing): https://www.uscloud.com/blog/ftc-microsoft-antitrust-investigation-continues-in-2026/

thesis: Lumentum reported FQ4 2026 on 11 August with revenue of $1,006.3M, up 109.3% year over year and the company's first billion-dollar quarter, with adjusted EPS and revenue roughly doubling year over year and beating estimates, and Q1 guidance above expectations; the stock rose about 13.6% the following session and multiple banks raised targets. This is a confirmed, company-disclosed result rather than a rumour or a sector move, and it accounts for the +12.3% 60-day move. The counter-case of customer concentration — roughly 40% of the business, weighted to NVIDIA and Apple — is partly answered by NVIDIA's own Q2 FY2027 disclosure on 26 August guiding Q3 revenue to $108.0B, which indicates the largest customer's demand is still expanding. What this run's research cannot settle is valuation: analysts put the stock at roughly 145x trailing and 84x forward earnings, with at least one published fair-value model implying material downside, and no source read here resolves whether that multiple is supportable. The read is therefore a confirmed operational beat carrying an unresolved valuation counter-case.
invalidation: Q1 FY2027 revenue comes in below the guided range, or NVIDIA/Apple order commentary points to a smaller optical content roadmap.
sources: TradingKey (LITE Q4 FY2026 results and 12 Aug move): https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262100076-market-movers-lite-20260812

thesis: Marvell released Q2 FY2027 results on 27 August: record revenue of $2.739B against $2.71B expected, non-GAAP EPS of $0.94 against $0.92 expected, and GAAP net income of $308M or $0.33 per diluted share (both metrics reported, and they differ substantially). The company raised its annual outlook for a second consecutive quarter and guided Q3 to revenue of $3.15B plus or minus 5% with non-GAAP EPS of $1.10 plus or minus five cents, citing broad-based Data Center strength and acceleration in its Custom business. This is a confirmed, company-disclosed beat and raise. The counter-case is the one the market was already trading: the stock gave up ground for three sessions into the print specifically on margin expectations, and it entered the report up 179% year to date. This run's research could not settle it — no source read here reports the quarter's gross margin or the margin embedded in the Q3 guide — so the margin question that drove the pre-print weakness remains open even though the revenue and EPS lines beat.
invalidation: Q3 revenue tracks below the $3.15B midpoint, or subsequent disclosure shows custom-silicon mix compressing gross margin.

thesis: Held position. Dell's most recently reported quarter carried record revenue of $43.8B, up 88%, and record EPS of $4.86, up 214%, with $24.4B of AI orders, $16.1B of AI server revenue and a record $51.3B backlog; management raised full-year revenue guidance to $165B-$169B and projected roughly $60B of AI server revenue for the year. The 13.9% 60-day move includes a roughly 10% single-session gain on 12 August that coverage attributed to read-through from CoreWeave and Super Micro results rather than to a Dell disclosure. The position sits 8.4% below its 52-week high. The decisive open item is that Dell reports again on 1 September, within days and well before this position's next likely review, so the disclosed strength has not yet been re-tested against a fresh quarter; that unresolved binary is why this is not rated higher despite a confirmed, company-specific catalyst. No litigation naming the company surfaced in this run's research.
invalidation: The 1 September report shows AI server backlog shrinking or the full-year $165B-$169B revenue guidance being walked back.

thesis: Held position. Astera Labs reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $392.4M, up 104% year over year on Scorpio X-Series fabric switch demand, and guided Q3 to $540M-$560M. Against that, the position is down 33.3% over 60 days and sits 39.1% below its 52-week high. This run's research does not reconcile those two facts. The only company-specific pressure it surfaced is mid-July insider selling: SEC filings show Board Chairman Manuel Alba and Director Stefan Dyckerhoff executing multi-million-dollar automated divestments under Rule 10b5-1 plans. Scheduled 10b5-1 sales do not plausibly account for a third of the market value, and no disclosed operational deterioration, guidance cut, offering or legal action naming the company turned up. The tape is therefore saying something the disclosed facts as gathered here do not explain, and the held-position search budget for this cycle is spent, so this is logged as unresolved rather than resolved in either direction. Nothing found supports exiting; nothing found explains the drawdown.
invalidation: Q3 revenue comes in below the guided $540M-$560M range, or a disclosure emerges showing customer or design-win loss behind the drawdown.
sources: Simply Wall St (Q2 2026 revenue $392.4M, Q3 guide): https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/semiconductors/nasdaq-alab/astera-labs

thesis: Held position. The position is up 33.0% over 60 days and sits 7.6% below its 52-week high, with the bulk of that gain arriving in a single session on 30 July on roughly 2.9M shares against a ~555k 30-bar average. This run's research did not identify the catalyst for that session, so the move driving the position's gain is unconfirmed rather than explained. What research did confirm is the standing overhang: a putative securities class action covering 31 October 2024 to 30 December 2025 alleges Corcept failed to disclose FDA concerns about the adequacy of relacorilant's hypertension programme and the GRACE trial design, with three groups of stockholders filing lead-plaintiff motions on 21 April 2026; separately, on 19 February 2026 the appellate court affirmed the district court's finding of no infringement of either patent in Corcept's case against Teva over generic Korlym. No scheduled ruling, hearing, trial date or compliance deadline in the next ~90 days was found for either matter, so active_litigation is not flagged. Nothing found indicates deterioration that would end the holding, but the gain rests on a catalyst this run could not source.
invalidation: A lead-plaintiff appointment or scheduling order sets a near-term litigation date, or the unexplained 30 July move proves to have been a one-off that reverses.
sources: PR Newswire (securities class action, class period, lead plaintiff motions): https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/corcept-therapeutics-incorporated-cort-shareholders-who-lost-money-have-opportunity-to-lead-securities-fraud-lawsuit-302742281.html

Hagens Berman alert (FDA rejection and patent loss): https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/cort-shareholder-alert-hagens-berman-alerts-corcept-therapeutics-cort--investors-to-securities-class-action-following-fda-rejection-and-federal-court-patent-loss-302746597.html

thesis: Corning's 40.2% 60-day decline has more than one driver and this run's research resolves none of them into a single dominant cause. Q2 2026 (28 July) was a beat on both lines: core EPS of $0.78, up 30% year over year, against $0.76 expected, and core sales of $4.74B, up 17%, against $4.63B expected, with Optical Communications sales of $2.07B, up 32% year over year but decelerating from 36% the prior quarter. The sell-off came on guidance, with Q3 core sales guided to $4.9B-$5.0B against $4.99B expected, and shares fell about 14% premarket. Separately, the 1 July drop of roughly 13% is attributed to a valuation unwind after the trailing P/E passed 105x, alongside Form 4 insider sales of over 160,000 shares by the CEO and several SVPs in mid-to-late June, and an August leg lower followed reports that Apple scrapped its all-glass anniversary iPhone. A beat, a light sales guide, a technical de-rating from an extreme multiple and a customer design loss point in different directions, and the mechanical component means the move is not a clean read on the business.
invalidation: Q3 core sales land above the guided $4.9B-$5.0B range with Optical Communications growth re-accelerating, which would mark the de-rating as complete.

thesis: Rocket Lab's Q2 2026 report (11 August) paired record revenue of $234M, up 62% year over year, and a $2.36B backlog with disclosures that cut the other way: non-GAAP free cash flow of -$110.1M driven by Neutron tail production, the Mynaric integration and SDA programme buildout, Q3 guidance of $250M-$265M with gross margin of 29%-31% and widening adjusted EBITDA losses, and CEO Peter Beck stating that the window for a Neutron first flight before the end of 2026 is narrowing. The stock fell roughly 10% and is down 31.1% over 60 days, sitting 55.1% below its 52-week high. The evidence is genuinely offsetting rather than resolved: the revenue and backlog trajectory is strong, and the cash burn has no relief until Neutron flies successfully, with the timing of that flight the very thing management is now hedging. This suggests the record top line does not settle the question the market is pricing.
invalidation: Neutron completes a successful first flight, or free cash flow turns materially less negative without it.
sources: TrendSpider (Q2 beat, Neutron timeline slip, FCF -$110.1M): https://trendspider.com/blog/rklb-stock-q2-earnings-neutron-delay/

thesis: Intel is down 30.1% over 60 days on company-specific disclosures rather than a rumour. A $20B secondary equity offering is creating an ongoing supply overhang, with the stock trading below its offering price after failing to hold $100, and Intel Foundry posted a $2.8B operating loss in Q2 2026. Coverage also reports CPU market share at a three-decade low with AMD EPYC taking 34% of server share. Those are disclosed structural problems — dilution plus a loss-making foundry plus share erosion — that compound rather than offset each other, and 24 August's decline came with a broader semiconductor sell-off on top. This run did not engage and dismiss a counter-case: reported government/strategic investment interest exists but this research did not establish whether it changes the dilution or foundry economics, so the negative read is credible but not stress-tested.
invalidation: Foundry operating losses narrow materially in a subsequent quarter, or the offering overhang clears with the stock holding above the offering price.
sources: FX Leaders (CPU share, AMD EPYC server share): https://www.fxleaders.com/news/2026/08/24/can-80-support-hold-intc-stock-as-the-intel-cpu-market-share-hits-3-decade-low-despite-pelosi-investment/

thesis: AST SpaceMobile is down 29.2% over 60 days and sits 54.1% below its 52-week high, but the drivers this run found are competitive and sentiment-driven rather than a disclosed deterioration at the company. Shares fell after SpaceX announced structural changes to its launch schedule, with its VP of Launch confirming that pad 40's mission was the last planned Falcon 9 Starlink launch from Florida and that Starlink missions there will move to Starship; coverage also cites broad space-sector weakness, profit-taking, analyst commentary that a potential SpaceX IPO could prompt institutional rebalancing away from ASTS, and Starlink's expanding direct-to-cell capability. The one concrete regulatory item is that the FCC granted only a temporary 30-day authorisation restricted to non-commercial 800 MHz testing. The move is therefore largely sector- and competitor-driven, which discounts its weight as a read on this company's own execution.
invalidation: The FCC grants commercial 800 MHz authorisation, or the company discloses constellation milestones that decouple it from SpaceX-driven sector sentiment.

thesis: SanDisk is down 27.6% over 60 days, but this run's research attributes the largest part of that to mechanics rather than to the business. The stock fell 56.49% from a 25 June close of $2,335.00 to $1,015.89 on 29 July, then closed up 25.99% the very next session, and coverage states the July collapse had little to do with the company's fundamentals and a lot to do with one leveraged fund. The August leg is different in kind: shares fell about 6.45% on 24 August on a report that the administration may permit Apple to source memory from Chinese suppliers CXMT and YMTC, a media report rather than a company disclosure. Against that, fiscal Q3 2026 revenue was $5.95B with GAAP EPS of $23.03 against $14.18 expected, and supply agreements are reported to carry a floor price near $0.29 per gigabyte. A forced-unwind drawdown plus an unconfirmed policy report does not add up to a disclosed fundamental deterioration, and equally does not establish that the de-rating is finished.
invalidation: The Apple/CXMT/YMTC sourcing report is confirmed or refuted by a company or government statement, which would replace the current mechanical read with a fundamental one.
sources: TIKR (55% drawdown, leveraged fund unwind, 26% rebound): https://www.tikr.com/blog/sandisk-stock-fell-55-from-its-june-high-then-ripped-26-in-a-day-heres-where-the-stock-could-go-in-2026
Motley Fool (24 Aug drop, Apple/CXMT/YMTC report): https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/24/why-sandisk-stock-dropped-this-morning/

thesis: Coherent is down 24.5% over 60 days, and the research this run found points to a sector-wide de-rating rather than a company-specific deterioration. Shares fell 14.23% on 10 August ahead of the print as a crowded AI-optics trade unwound, after a week in which the stock had gained 44%. The fiscal Q4 2026 results on 12 August were not weak in absolute terms: revenue of $2.05B, up 34% year over year, with non-GAAP EPS of $1.74, and FQ1 2027 guidance of $2.2B-$2.4B revenue and $1.85-$2.05 non-GAAP EPS alongside commentary on strong demand and expanding capacity. Coverage read the continued pressure as a broad selloff across optical and photonics names and a reassessment of valuation and competitive risk across AI networking, not a new company-specific negative. A move explained principally by sector rotation and multiple compression is a weak basis for a directional read on the business.
invalidation: FQ1 2027 revenue lands outside the guided $2.2B-$2.4B range, which would convert a sector de-rating into a company-specific problem.
sources: 24/7 Wall St (10 Aug 14.23% decline, AI optics unwind): https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/10/coherent-cohr-stock-is-tumbling-today-after-massive-optics-vs-memory-debate-on-social-media-this-weekend/

thesis: Applied Optoelectronics announced another $600M at-the-market equity offering around 21-24 August and the stock fell about 10% after hours, with the close dropping from $124.82 on 21 August to $107.63 on 24 August. That is a specific, confirmed, company-disclosed action, and it is the proximate driver of the recent leg down within a 24.5% 60-day decline. The strongest counter-evidence is that the operating business is not the problem: Q2 2026 (6 August) delivered a fifth consecutive record quarter with revenue of $191.9M, up 86% year over year, EPS of $0.06 against $0.01 expected, and Q3 guidance of $255M-$290M revenue with adjusted EPS of $0.11-$0.26 as 800G and 1.6T products ramp. That does not change the near-term read, because a $600M ATM is an immediate and quantified supply of new shares that lands regardless of how the order book develops, and it arrives after a roughly 45% run from 20 July to 14 August rather than from a depressed base. The counter-case is not dismissed outright, only outweighed for a short holding period, which is why this is not rated higher.
invalidation: The ATM programme is completed or withdrawn without further share issuance, or Q3 revenue lands above the guided $255M-$290M range with the offering already absorbed.
sources: Timothy Sykes (record AI revenue, 14 Aug close $149.10): https://www.timothysykes.com/news/applied-optoelectronics-inc-aaoi-news-2026_08_14/

thesis: Micron is down 18.3% over 60 days on two drivers this run could not reduce to one. The first is a media report, not a company disclosure: WCCTech reported the administration has decided to permit Apple to buy memory from Chinese suppliers CXMT and YMTC, and the stock fell 5.5% in the first five minutes of trading on 24 August. The second is a specific legal filing: Netlist filed a complaint with the US International Trade Commission on 12 August against Micron and others alleging infringement of four patents tied to DDR5 RDIMM and MRDIMM products. Coverage separately flags analyst concern that DRAM and NAND pricing power may peak earlier than expected against roughly $27B of fiscal 2026 capital expenditure on greenfield fabs, which raises operating leverage if supply normalises. An unconfirmed policy report, an unscheduled ITC action and a pricing-cycle debate are three separate open questions rather than one settled read. No scheduled ITC ruling, hearing or deadline within the next ~90 days surfaced in this run's research.
invalidation: The Apple/CXMT/YMTC sourcing decision is officially confirmed or denied, or the ITC institutes an investigation with a scheduled target date.
sources: Motley Fool (24 Aug decline, WCCTech Apple/CXMT/YMTC report): https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/24/why-micron-stock-dropped-this-morning/

thesis: Nebius announced a $4.5B capital raise through a private offering of convertible senior notes — $2.75B due 2030 and $1.75B due 2034 — to fund its AI data centre build-out, and the stock fell as much as 14% on the announcement and a further 4% as the deal settled in late August, contributing to a 16.3% 60-day decline. That is a confirmed, company-disclosed financing action rather than a rumour. The counter-evidence is substantial and this run cannot rank it against the dilution: Q2 2026 revenue was $582.3M, up 454% year over year, with $37.5B of remaining performance obligations, and the stock was still up 174% year to date after the sell-off. Coverage also notes a contentious public hearing over construction of one of its data centres. A convertible structure of this size against an RPO of that size is offsetting rather than decisive evidence, and this research does not settle which dominates over a short holding period.
invalidation: The convertible notes convert or are refinanced without further dilution, or RPO conversion into recognised revenue visibly accelerates.
sources: Motley Fool (Q2 revenue $582.3M, RPO $37.5B, risk profile): https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/21/nebius-stock-a-high-risk-high-reward-investment/

thesis: SpaceX is down 14.2% over 60 days and roughly 39% from its all-time high of $225.64, trading less than 3% above its $135 IPO price. Its Q2 2026 report — the first since the June IPO — beat on revenue but the stock fell about 8% in extended trading as capital expenditure jumped more than sixfold year over year to $18.37B, of which $15.83B was AI, with net income at a loss of $541M and a pretax margin around -38.3%. Those are disclosed figures. The read is not clean, though: a revenue beat sits directly against a capex step-change and a widening loss, and coverage attributes part of the continued weakness to macro conditions — higher oil prices, geopolitical tension and inflation worries hitting the growth complex — rather than to the company. A company-disclosed spending decision and a risk-off macro tape are pulling in the same direction here without either being established as dominant.
invalidation: A subsequent quarter shows capital expenditure moderating with the loss narrowing, or the stock decouples from the broader growth complex.
sources: Motley Fool (39% drawdown from peak, IPO price context): https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/26/spacex-stock-has-pulled-back-39-from-its-peak-and/
Timothy Sykes (spending and macro pressure, net loss and margin): https://www.timothysykes.com/news/space-exploration-technologies-corp-spcx-news-2026_08_24/

thesis: Cerebras is down 13.6% over 60 days and sits 15.3% above its 52-week low. Both metrics from the Q2 2026 report are reported here because they diverge sharply: revenue of $180.11M missed the $193.55M analyst estimate, and GAAP EPS of -$2.98 came in far below the -$0.18 consensus, with shares falling 26.41% in a single week afterwards. Two further disclosed items weigh: the lock-up is easing, with co-founder and CTO Sean Lie filing to sell over $153M of shares and executive lock-ups running until the earlier of the second trading day after Q3 2026 earnings or 9 November, and the pivot to building its own data centres raises capital intensity. Against that sit genuinely positive company events — the CS-4 launch at Supernova 2026, a Callosum inference partnership, a ten-year CleanCore colocation deal, AMD integration, ARK buying $8.84M on 18 August and a Morgan Stanley overweight — plus a $25.4B RPO. The gap between that RPO and Q3 guidance of only $214M-$216M is precisely what this run cannot resolve: a large backlog whose recognition pace is unknown, set against a confirmed earnings miss and insider supply.
invalidation: Q3 revenue converts RPO materially faster than the guided $214M-$216M, or the lock-up passes without significant insider supply.
sources: Seeking Alpha (Q2 miss, GAAP EPS -$2.98, RPO vs Q3 guide, lock-up): https://seekingalpha.com/article/4940809-cerebras-still-has-a-promising-future-but-there-is-still-limited-evidence

Stocktwits (CTO Sean Lie filing to sell $153M, lock-up terms): https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/cerebras-cto-files-to-sell-over-153-m-stock-senior-executives-offload-small-lots/cZYB8DJRJNQ

thesis: AMD is down 11.6% over 60 days, and the cause this run's research identifies is predominantly sector-wide rather than company-specific. The shares fell about 18% across July in a semiconductor sell-off driven by fears of AI overspending, during which the largest semiconductor stocks lost a collective $1 trillion in market capitalisation. Company-adjacent items exist but are reports rather than company disclosures: coverage cites a report that DeepSeek is developing its own AI processor, and a report that a major customer would source AI chips from a rival. The company's own reported results run the other way, with revenue up 50% year over year and data center sales more than doubling, and the stock remains up over 108% year to date against a trailing P/E of 123. A broad rotation out of the AI complex against strong disclosed results is a valuation and sentiment story, not a deterioration this research can pin to the business.
invalidation: A confirmed customer loss or a guidance cut replaces the sector-rotation explanation with a company-specific one.
sources: Motley Fool (18% July decline, AI overspending sell-off, DeepSeek and customer reports): https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/10/why-amd-stock-tumbled-18-in-july/
